title: Consumer complaint after 2-year limit

input.title: Consumer complaint after 2-year limit
turns: I bought a washing machine for 30,000 in March 2023 and it stopped working in April 2023. The company never fixed it. Can I file a consumer case now?

turns.user: I bought a washing machine for 30,000 in March 2023 and it stopped working in April 2023. The company never fixed it. Can I file a consumer case now?
turns.reply:
**What I understood**
You bought a washing machine for Rs 30,000 in March 2023, but it broke down in April 2023 and the company never fixed it.

**Where you stand**
The usual time limit to file a consumer complaint is 2 years from the date the problem arose [K:cpa-limitation]. For your case, that deadline passed on April 1, 2025. Because the time limit has passed, you generally cannot file a standard case unless the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission agrees to excuse the delay for a very good reason. 

**What you can do now**
1. Talk to a lawyer or your local District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) by calling the NALSA helpline at 15100 to see if your delay can be excused [K:legal-aid].
2. You can still try calling the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 to see if they can help resolve the issue with the company informally [K:nch].

**What I still need from you**
1. Do you have the purchase invoice or bill?
2. Do you have any old emails, chat records, or service ticket numbers showing you complained to the company earlier?

**When to get a real lawyer**
You should speak to a lawyer immediately because your time limit to file a consumer case has already passed, and you will need legal help to ask the Commission for an extension.

case.user_goal: File a consumer case to get a refund or resolution for the defective washing machine.

deadlines.label: Last date to file a consumer complaint (2 years)

escalations.reason: The usual time limit (last date to file a consumer complaint (2 years)) passed on 2025-04-01.
escalations.action: Only the court or Commission can excuse the delay, and you must show a good reason - see a lawyer or DLSA (15100) quickly.

missing: Proof of payment (UPI / card / bank statement)
Complaint to the company and their reply (emails, chats, ticket numbers)
Photos / videos of the defect or problem
Warranty card / terms promised at sale

ladder: Write to the company's customer care / grievance officer and keep the ticket number.
Register a free complaint with the National Consumer Helpline (pre-litigation mediation).
Send a written demand / legal notice giving a clear deadline (usually 15 days).
File a complaint before the District Consumer Commission (online filing possible; no lawyer needed).
